title: A temporal filter removes inferred decay at short lags in three linear connectome models
abstract: We tested directed drift recovery from exact lagged covariance in three linear stochastic graph models. The graphs represent 302 worm neurons, 75 fly regions and 304 Allen-based mouse parcels. We used two recurrent gains and three common first-order filter times. For a differentiable stationary signal, the zero-lag covariance derivative is skew symmetric. A drift estimate that ignores the filter therefore has zero trace in the short-lag limit. All 18 model settings passed this check. At gain 0.8 and lag 0.001, mean inferred decay was 0.00010 to 0.00250, compared with the true value of 1. Off-diagonal coupling error was 0.775 to 0.983 in relative Frobenius norm. An identity using the known filter and derivatives through third order recovered drift with error below 1e-15 over 72 positive-lag tests. This is an exact-covariance model audit, not a fit to measured activity or a test of statistical robustness. Unknown filters and noisy derivatives remain open problems. Code, proof, aggregate scores, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. External graphs stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Mean inferred decay at four lags for gain 0.8 in three graph models. Each true neural decay is 1. A smaller lag does not remove an ignored filter. Filter times and lags are in neural decay units.
